stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $81,000 after the Nasdaq's worst day since June
stories.summary: Bitcoin gave back Wednesday's jump toward $85,000 and traded around $81,000 after the US stock market closed on Thursday. Tech stocks fell as Meta's results revived worries about AI spending, and oil climbed after Houthi strikes on Saudi targets, per Yahoo Finance. Smaller coins and DeFi tokens fell more than bitcoin. Crypto has been moving with tech stocks this week, and when prices drop fast, traders who borrowed to bet on a rise get forced out, which adds to the fall.
points: The Nasdaq closed down 2.60% at 26,008.86, its worst day since early June; the S&P 500 fell 1.21% and the Dow was flat, per Yahoo Finance.
Meta closed down 7.84% per Sharecast (Yahoo Finance says about 7%); Brent oil rose 3.83% to $112.99, per Sharecast.
In the Bloomberg markets wrap (20:57 UTC), bitcoin was at $81,350, down 3.9%, and ether at $2,383, down 4.3%.
Forced closures of leveraged bets: CoinDesk put them at $431.1M; Bitcoin.com counted over $412M of bets on a rise and over $43M of bets on a fall across the market.
CoinDesk's DeFi index fell 5.6% and Curve 8.2%, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs took in about $1B in three days, but the price fell anyway
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, funds that hold bitcoin for stock-market investors, had three straight days of inflows from Monday to Wednesday, yet bitcoin still fell on Thursday. Thursday's flow figures were not out yet when this edition was written. Ether funds have had a much weaker month.
points: Wednesday's net inflow was $524.8M per Farside and $528.4M per The Block.
BlackRock's IBIT took in $235.0M and Fidelity's FBTC $212.7M on Wednesday, per Farside.
Monday to Wednesday added up to about $1.07B per Farside, and about $1.08B per SoSoValue (via Cointelegraph).
Spot ether ETFs had lost about $1.08B so far in October as of 21 Oct, the biggest monthly outflow of 2026, per SoSoValue via Cointelegraph.

stories.title: A Senate Democrat opens a probe into Tether payments, as US crypto rules shift to agencies
stories.summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal, the top Democrat on the Senate's main investigations subcommittee, sent letters to Tether and to Nxum Group, a consulting firm co-founded by Bo Hines, the former White House crypto adviser who now runs Tether's US arm. The letters ask about reported payments made while Hines was still advising the President. Meanwhile, with the broader crypto market bill stuck in Congress, most new US rules are coming from agencies, which future administrations can change.
points: Tether says an outside law firm "found no evidence of wrongdoing", per CoinDesk.
The OCC's final stablecoin rule runs 721 pages; it bars exchanges from paying yield just for holding stablecoins, and the American Bankers Association objects to it, per Roll Call.
JPMorgan analysts say agency actions only partly make up for the stalled CLARITY Act, which they expect to slip possibly into 2027, per The Block.
The Blockchain Association is asking Congress for a de minimis exemption, meaning no tax on very small crypto transactions, per The Block.

briefs.title: China moves to claim $5.1B of UK-held bitcoin
briefs.summary: Prosecutors in Tianjin want to confiscate 61,896 BTC tied to fraudster Zhimin Qian. A six-month notice period runs before a court hearing.

briefs.title: Bitcoin's share of the crypto market nears 60%
briefs.summary: Bitcoin dominance is at its highest since May as traders move out of smaller coins; memecoins fell more than 5%, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Monero rises against the trend
briefs.summary: XMR rose about 12% to around $648 with no confirmed reason, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Kalshi offers crypto-backed loans; Webull plans crypto perpetual futures
briefs.summary: Kalshi Prime clients can borrow against BTC, ETH and stablecoins held at BitGo. Webull plans to launch US crypto perpetual futures in November through Kalshi's CFTC-regulated exchange.

briefs.title: Underdog to accept crypto deposits for prediction markets
briefs.summary: Eligible users will be able to fund accounts with stablecoins and other crypto through Zerohash, expected before the end of 2026. Those holdings have no FDIC or SIPC protection.

briefs.title: New York's attorney general also asks the SEC to pull its crypto rule
briefs.summary: A 20 Oct letter urges the SEC to withdraw its proposed 'Regulation Crypto Assets', per a Lowenstein Sandler brief.

briefs.title: Coinbase Ireland fined about $3.6M
briefs.summary: The Central Bank of Ireland fined it €3.25M over failures to keep customer funds separate and oversee the business properly.
